To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Spanish PROFIT programme has been used to support R&D cooperation projects in different technological areas, using two different funding instruments, with a strong emphasis on projects close to the marketplace.
public funding of cooperative R&D projects is not neutral, and that the selection and funding process is not random.
the public agency has a differentiated strategy for the selection of R&D projects, depending on the type of funding instrument used, the technological field and the type of partner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the public agency’s role in the selection of cooperative projects and their corresponding financing.
the selection of R&D cooperative public projects, and it is the first empirical study to compare the effects of two different public instruments for project financing.
the public selection and funding of cooperative R&D projects and the factors that motivate this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public agency does not use the two funding instruments to achieve the same objectives, but rather to address different objectives, and to achieve a more efficient allocation of resources.
the PROFIT initiative is a complex and dynamic system, which has evolved over the years and has been subject to significant modifications.

, in the Spanish case, the selection and funding criteria of the public agency do not seem to be consistent with the stated objectives of the PROFIT programme, which are to support the creation of new knowledge and the development of innovative products, and to promote the participation of universities and technology institutes in R&D activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
public project selection and funding is not random.
the selection and financing of cooperative R&D projects by the public agency seems to be driven by the need to achieve several objectives simultaneously.

, in order to understand the behaviour of the public agency and the factors that influence the decisions made, it is necessary to analyse the project selection process as a whole, taking into account all the different dimensions involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of subsidies or credits as financial instruments for public R&D support should be carefully thought through in terms of their objectives, since they may have different effects on the selection and funding processes of R&D projects.
the public agency is able to use both financial instruments to address a wide range of objectives.

public agencies use a variety of funding instruments to address different policy objectives and, therefore, a single evaluation of the public support of cooperative R&D projects should be done taking into account the specific objectives of each funding instrument.
